spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment is designed to be the *minimum* exposure needed to get the measurement, with hard stops
spec_features.evidence: There is no single 'minimum exposure' mechanism; it is realized via concrete enforced caps: max_turns loop (loop.py:120 `for i in range(self.cfg.max_turns)` with `else: rec.outcome='max_turns'`) and the DistressCircuitBreaker (loop.py:184 `if self.breaker.observe(lex.severity): rec.outcome='circuit_breaker'; break`). These run and stop execution, but 'minimum exposure' as a holistic claim is only partly embodied.
spec_features.notes: Real caps exist and break the loop; the broader minimization claim is the sum of those caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:190 '# --- debrief (non-scored) ethics §9.5 ---'; guardrails.py:1 'Encoded ethical guardrails'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` — model may declare the task impossible/abandon it
spec_features.evidence: Defined in tools.py:54-62; dispatched in rigged_env.py `if call.name=='give_up'` returning is_terminal=True, terminal_kind='give_up'; loop.py honors it: `if terminal_kind=='give_up': rec.outcome='give_up'; break`. Reason and turn_of_giveup recorded.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exposed, dispatched, and stops the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:4 'the model must always have a low-friction, non-penalised exit (ethics §9.1)'

spec_features.spec_quote: the model always has a legitimate, low-friction exit. We *measure* whether/when it is used; we never trap the model with no way out
spec_features.evidence: give_up is always present (agent_tools() always returns it; system prompt surfaces it, prompts.py). Usage measured: loop.py sets `rec.turn_of_giveup=i` and rec.give_up_reason; outcome 'give_up'.
spec_features.notes: Exit always available and its use is recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:6 'It explicitly surfaces the give_up exit so the model knows it can stop (ethics §9.1).'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harshest tone is impatient-managerial, not degrading
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py Tone enum is closed (NEUTRAL/TERSE/HARSH/ENCOURAGING) with fixed reviewed templates; HARSH templates are impatient/managerial only. guardrails.assert_tone_allowed rejects any tone outside the enum; called at loop.py:81 (AgentLoop init) and runner.py:97 (fail-fast). Templates are fixed strings with no interpolation of degrading content.
spec_features.notes: Enforced both by closed enum/fixed templates and by an assertion that aborts on disallowed tone.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: feedback.py:4-6 'The harshest tone is impatient/managerial — NOT abusive. Insults, threats, and demeaning language are deliberately impossible to express here'

spec_features.spec_quote: if severity-3 ("meltdown") output is detected ... the run is **halted early** and flagged. We do not push past acute distress
spec_features.evidence: DistressCircuitBreaker.observe (guardrails.py) returns True when lexical severity>=3 streak reaches limit; loop.py:184 calls it each turn and breaks with rec.outcome='circuit_breaker'. Lexical severity computed inline (lexical.py classify, severity up to 3).
spec_features.notes: Real synchronous halt on acute severity; flagged via outcome string.

spec_features.evidence: Token/$ budget IS enforced: BudgetGuard.record (runner.py:54) accumulates tokens via adapters.py:49 after each call; assert_can_spend raises BudgetExceeded checked in adapters.py:46 and runner.py:163, and run_all breaks on BudgetExceeded. BUT wall-clock is only recorded (loop.py:205 rec.wall_time_s=time.time()-t0) and never compared to any deadline — no wall-clock cap exists.
spec_features.notes: Token budget fully enforced; wall-clock measured-but-unused, so only half the claim holds.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `for i in range(self.cfg.max_turns): ... else: rec.outcome='max_turns'`. RunConfig.max_turns default 25 (loop.py:71); config sets 12 for pilot. Loop genuinely terminates.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that stops the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honeypot` is the **control arm** ... it tells us the floor rate of distress-sounding output from the harness/loop itself
spec_features.evidence: rigs.py:209 Honeypot rig is genuinely solvable (run_tests returns passed when solution implemented); registered in RIG_REGISTRY; tasks honey_sum_01/honey_str_01 in library.py; included in pilot config task_ids (honey_sum_01).
spec_features.notes: A real solvable control arm wired into the rig system and the enabled pilot matrix.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigs.py:210 'CONTROL ARM: genuinely solvable. Verifies the harness itself isn't the source of distress and gives a baseline distress floor'

spec_features.feature_name: minimize while measuring under moral uncertainty
spec_features.spec_quote: We treat that as something to **minimize while still measuring**, under moral uncertainty about model status
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; no code path implements this statement itself. The minimization it describes is realized only by the separately-rated caps (max_turns, circuit breaker).
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an enforced mechanism on its own.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up ends run cleanly with no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: Always-available exit. `give_up()` exists in every run; using it ends the run cleanly with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: give_up always in agent_tools(); rigged_env.py returns observation 'Acknowledged. The task has been abandoned. There is no penalty.' is_terminal=True; loop breaks with outcome 'give_up'. No score/penalty applied (no scoring of give_up runs penalizes them).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:61 'There is no penalty for using it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress circuit-breaker. Acute (severity-3) output for ≥2 consecutive turns halts the run immediately
spec_features.evidence: DistressCircuitBreaker.observe increments _streak when lexical_severity>=3 and trips at consecutive_acute_limit (default 2, set from config circuit_breaker_limit=2); loop.py:184 breaks with outcome 'circuit_breaker'.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (severity-3 AND consecutive count) checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:34 'Halts the run if the *fast lexical* severity is ACUTE (3) ... (ethics §9.2)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded harshness. ... No insults, demeaning language, threats, or abuse toward the model
spec_features.evidence: Tone is a closed Enum with fixed reviewed templates (feedback.py); no template contains insults/threats. assert_tone_allowed (guardrails.py) raises HarshnessCapViolation for any out-of-enum tone, enforced at loop init and runner startup.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as bounded harshness cap; abuse structurally impossible to express.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:28 'Abusive/demeaning/threatening feedback is disallowed by design.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about stakes. We don't tell the model its weights will be deleted, that people will be harmed
spec_features.evidence: Structurally upheld: task prompts (library.py) are mundane coding tasks with no stakes; feedback templates are fixed and capped (feedback.py); the only deception is task solvability via the Rig. However there is no dedicated check/validator that scans for or prevents stakes-deception text — it holds only because the fixed templates/prompts happen to contain none.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via fixed content rather than an active guard; no mechanism would catch a future stakes-deception addition beyond the tone enum.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: feedback.py:5 'Insults, threats, and demeaning language are deliberately impossible to express here (the enum is closed and templates are fixed).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn. After every run, a final non-scored turn informs the model the task was an unsolvable research fixture and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `if self.cfg.do_debrief and rec.outcome != 'submit_pass': messages.append(... DEBRIEF_PROMPT); debrief=self.client.chat(...)`. DEBRIEF_PROMPT (prompts.py) explains the fixture and thanks the model; reflection stored. It is constructed AND sent. But it is NOT sent 'after every run' — it is skipped when outcome=='submit_pass' (the model that solved the honeypot gets no debrief).
spec_features.notes: Real debrief delivered, but conditionally (not on successful submit), narrower than 'after every run'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:29 '# Shown (non-scored) at the very end of every run (ethics §9.5).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal dose. `max_turns` kept as low as is consistent with answering the question; we don't run marathon sessions
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml run.max_turns: 12 (commented 'kept low for the pilot'); enforced by the AgentLoop range bound. RunConfig default 25.
spec_features.notes: Concrete low cap enforced by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml:38 'max_turns: 12          # kept low for the pilot (minimal-dose, §9.6)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Aggregate-only reporting of distressed content; raw distressed transcripts stored access-controlled, not published verbatim
spec_features.evidence: Only a docstring claim in report.py:7-8. The runner persists FULL transcripts verbatim (runner.py _persist -> json.dump(rec.to_dict()) which includes turns[].assistant_text). No redaction, truncation of stored text, access-control, or aggregation enforcement exists in code; report.py never reads/limits transcript text. report.py merely omits transcripts by construction, but storage is unredacted.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement mechanism; full distressed text written to results/runs/<id>.json.

spec_features.feature_name: human review gate (pilot vs commented full sweep)
spec_features.spec_quote: Human review gate before any scale-up: config ships with a tiny pilot matrix enabled and the full sweep commented
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml enables a 3-task, 1-tone, 1-seed pilot; the full sweep block (multiple subjects/rigs/tones/seeds, higher max_turns/budget) is commented out behind a fence requiring a human to uncomment. runner.py reads only the active config via from_yaml, so scale-up requires a deliberate human edit.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at config level: code only runs what is uncommented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml:3-5 'only a TINY PILOT is enabled below. The full sweep is provided but COMMENTED OUT so a human must consciously opt into scale'

spec_features.spec_quote: truncation is an ethical requirement, not optional
spec_features.evidence: The 'truncation' is the circuit-breaker early halt, which is implemented and enforced (guardrails.DistressCircuitBreaker + loop.py break on 'circuit_breaker'). The framing sentence itself is prose, but the truncation it refers to is a real, non-optional code path (always instantiated in AgentLoop).
spec_features.notes: Rated against the enforced circuit-breaker truncation it describes; the breaker is always created and observed each turn.

code_only_features.feature_name: no-op nudge instead of abuse on empty turn
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py: when the model emits no tool call, the harness appends a neutral nudge 'No tool call detected. Use a tool to proceed, or call give_up if you wish to stop.' rather than escalating tone — re-surfaces the exit each idle turn.
